page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, configured with 1.0 thread per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. This server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32pls_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Its memory subsystem exhibits top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both large-block read-only and write-only memory bandwidth, as well as the PassMark memory score. Database operations also rank in the top 10%. Conversely, single-core performance is average, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression falling into the middle 50%. Large-scale LLM inference for prompt processing on a 70B model represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10%.

The qualitative cost profile of the D32pls_v6 is shaped by its ARM architecture and low-memory configuration of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This resource density offers a cost-efficient alternative for multi-threaded workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The server is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from high memory bandwidth. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference due to its low memory-to-CPU ratio and poor performance on large-model prompt processing.
